hypotheses.justification: The statement only uses p as a natural number (p ∣ Nat.card D, p ^ (Nat.card C).factorization p) and never uses the Fact. The Fact is recoverable from [CharP k p] with [Field k]. Mathlib's `CharP.char_is_prime_or_zero` gives `Nat.Prime p ∨ p = 0`. If p is prime, the existing proof goes through after `haveI := Fact.mk hp`. If p = 0, take D = C. Then `D ≤ C` holds. `¬ 0 ∣ Nat.card C` holds because C is finite, so its cardinality is nonzero. `C.relIndex C = 1`, and `0 ^ ((Nat.card C).factorization 0) = 0 ^ 0 = 1`, since `Nat.factorization` at a non-prime is 0. The last equation becomes `indK0 … = 1 • indK0 …`, which is true. So the theorem stays true and provable with `Fact p.Prime` omitted. I did not check each lemma in the p = 0 case against Lean, so this is the one point I am less sure of. CharP k p is genuinely needed: in characteristic 0 the statement fails, for example G = C = Z/p over Q.
